title: New class subcritical-turbulence (Barkley's pipe-flow model on a 2D strip): from random turbulent patches, puffs condense, travel slower than the bulk and persist as a regularly spaced train set by their own wakes; no splits or decays after the first ~150 t at r 0.7-0.87
summary: world.py is Barkley's two-field model (q turbulence, u centreline velocity; eps1 0.04, eps2 0.2, delta 0.1) in the bulk frame on a periodic 32 x 512 strip, with multiplicative noise on q. From random turbulent patches over the whole strip, q condenses within ~150 t into 2 (r 0.7) to 4-5 (r 0.8-0.87) strip-spanning puffs that drift upstream at a common speed, each followed by a depleted-u wake (screen_*.png, space-time panels); r 0.9 fills the strip, r 0.5 leaves one puff. labkit (r 0.8, sigma 0.6, seeds 0 and 1, T=1500): 4 and 3 persistent tracks that live the whole run, 0 persistent splits (5 short-lived threshold splits and 2-3 merges each, from noise at the puff edge).
limits: The box is crowded: in a periodic strip each puff lives in the wake of the one ahead, so the train's spacing, not splitting, sets the number; Barkley's splitting needs a puff with fully recovered flow upstream, which a much longer strip (or a sparser start) would give. The strip is 32 px high, so puffs span it and are effectively 1D bands; a wider strip may break them into spots or oblique bands. Noise only up to sigma 0.8; one seed in the screens. Not tried: a long strip (e.g. 16 x 4096), the label for heredity, the decay side (r < 0.7 with strong noise).
